correctness.rationale: Direct exact branch algebra gives slopes r, +s and −s and the exact switching points. The two inverse branches are strict separated contractions on J and their cylinders yield both the Cantor dimension and the geometric survival law. Every exit reaches the contracting scalar branch in at most two further steps, giving the exact basin. At endpoint r=0, two inverse images of each further survivor interval yield the full finite-capture tail. A checker independently verified 980 rational assertions, but the general results follow from the analytic proof. Endpoints and uniform measures are explicitly scoped.

value.rationale: This is a natural and commonly used predictive-feedback stabilizer rather than an artificial dynamical system. The gain-dependent dimension/entropy of all nonconvergent initial states and the dramatic transition from measure-zero finite-time capture to almost-sure finite-time capture at a distinguished stabilizing gain quantify actual control reliability beyond local stability or boundedness. The exact geometric first-exit and first-capture laws are structural, parameter-uniform outcomes for a complete interval, not arbitrary finite tables or a mere restatement of the generic IFS recipe.
